conviction_note: The one company-level number that decides the quarter, MIAX's own preliminary Q3 options RPC of $0.098 (IR file, 2026-10-06), is below management's August guide (~$0.103-0.11) and implies Q3 net revenue of about $127-128M against published consensus of $131.9-135.4M. But it has been public for 23 days, four brokers cut targets on it between Oct 7 and Oct 27, the stock is -9.9% over 5 days and -44.5% from its high, the skew pays for upside (-4.25), and the name has beaten EPS four quarters running with modest reactions. The bar is disputed (EPS $0.35/$0.40/$0.42), so every size is capped small. p_up is 47, with abs_move 6.5 below the 7.72 event-implied move because the name's own four reactions run at a 2.35 median. The scaled number (-0.39) and the findings sum (+0.4) disagree in sign but are both near zero: the findings carry a reset-expectations relief lean as a separate item, while p_up says the primary-document miss slightly outweighs it. That gap is information, not an inconsistency.
bar: Disputed, so capped. Q3 2026 net revenue $131.87M (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/MIAX) vs $135.4M (Benzinga, https://es.benzinga.com/quote/MIAX/earnings-forecasts). Adjusted EPS $0.40 at both of those sources, but $0.42 at TipRanks (https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/MIAX/earnings) and $0.35 (range $0.34-0.37, one analyst) at Tickflow (https://tickflow.io/stock/MIAX/forecast), per search snippets with no visible date stamps. FY2026 S&P consensus revenue is $534.6M, range $523.0-545.8M (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/miax/forecast/). That implies about $132M a quarter for H2 after H1 of $269.7M. The company gives no revenue guide, only expense guidance: adjusted opex $260-270M FY26 (https://www.miaxglobal.com/news/miami-international-holdings-reports-second-quarter-2026-results). print_vs_bar_pct is my revenue estimate of ~$127.5M against a ~$133M midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest 7,967,675 shares, 9.51% of float, 3.7 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15 (published 10/26), down 10.3% from 8.88M (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MIAX/short-interest). Elevated but not crowded. The baseline skew is -4.25 vol points (25d put IV below 25d call IV, so upside is paid), put/call OI is 0.12 on 3,937 contracts, and the ATM spread is 30% of mid, so the chain is thin and call-heavy. Event-implied move 7.72% against a 2.35% median of four prior reactions (-1.09, +4.36, +2.10, +2.60).

findings.finding: MIAX's own Volume & RPC report, updated 2026-10-06, carries a preliminary Q3'26 options RPC of $0.098, against $0.124 in Q2'26 and $0.110 in Q1'26. That is below the $0.103-0.11 management told the Q2 call to model for H2. The rolling three-month average fell every month, from $0.124 (Jun) to $0.117 (Jul), $0.107 (Aug) and $0.098 (Sep), which implies each Q3 month ran at roughly $0.095-0.10. Q3 options ADV was 11.088M over 64 days (Q2: 10.989M over 62), so options net transaction fees come to ~$69.5M against ~$84.5M in Q2. That puts Q3 net revenue near $127-128M against the published $131.9-135.4M consensus, about $0.03-0.05 of adjusted EPS below $0.40. Management attributed the decline to the July/August fee changes and the July 1 ORF change, so Q4 commentary on RPC is the forward line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 RPC upside ($0.124 vs ~$0.11) came with a 17% EPS beat ($0.48 vs $0.41) and the stock moved -1.09% (2026-08-05). Beats on 2026-05-06, 2026-02-25 and 2025-11-05 bought +4.36, +2.10 and +2.60. This name has paid little for the revenue line in either direction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is only partly unpriced. The figure sits in an IR spreadsheet PDF that no wire summarised: the September press release (Finviz/Grafa mirrors) carries no RPC, and Benzinga's $135.4M and TipRanks' $0.42 still look like pre-Oct-6 numbers. If the market had fully priced it, every consensus source would sit near $127M / $0.36. Instead they range $131.9-135.4M and $0.35-0.42. Against that, KBW cut its target to $35 on Oct 7 and Morgan Stanley to $43 on Oct 9, the day after the file, so the brokers who matter have seen it.
findings.independence: Management's own RPC guidance on the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-5-miami-international-holdings-inc-stock/) is the reference point it falls short of. The broker target cuts dated Oct 7-27 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/miax/forecast/) are consistent with estimates being lowered on this number. Same company document family, so not a second fact.

findings.finding: Q3'26 options volume and share were records in mix: market share 17.4% against 16.5% in Q2 (Jul 17.1%, Aug 18.4%, Sep 16.7%), ADV 11.088M, and YTD share a record 17.1% against 16.7%. Volume was not the problem; price was. A call that shows share holding while RPC stabilises is the upside case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 record share of 17.2% with a large EPS beat ($0.42 vs $0.30) bought +2.60% (2025-11-05).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: monthly volume releases are on the wire. Kept small because September share fell to 16.7% from 18.4% in August, the weakest exit rate of the quarter, which a market reading only the September release may have overweighted.
findings.independence: Shares the IR RPC file's volume rows. Same document family as finding 1, a different line (volume and share, not price).

findings.finding: Sell-side expectations were reset in the three weeks into the print. KBW cut its target $48 to $35 (Oct 7), Morgan Stanley $50 to $43 (Oct 9), J.P. Morgan $45 to $39 (Oct 26) and Rosenblatt $62 to $60 (Oct 27), while Piper Sandler held $52 (Oct 7). The stock fell 9.86% over the last 5 sessions to $31.54, 6.7% above its 52-week low, so the RPC disappointment has been marked down in price and in targets before the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print came into a pre-print drawdown of this size in the four-event history. The 2026-05-06 print (+4.36) is the largest positive reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is about what is priced, not new information. If the reset were not in the price, the stock would not be near its 52-week low after two late-October target cuts. The relief case is that a $0.36-0.38 print against a bar that has quietly moved down reads as in line.
findings.independence: AAII on 2026-10-29 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/549834-why-miami-international-holdings-inc8217s-miax-stock-is-down-589) records one downgrade and one upgrade in the past month and the stock down 5.64% for the month. The baseline 5d run-up of -9.86% is the tape.

findings.finding: Short interest of 9.51% of float (7.97M shares, 3.7 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15), down 10.3% from the prior settlement. Together with a call-heavy chain (put/call OI 0.12, 25d skew -4.25, upside paid), this means the marginal holder into the print is positioned for upside and a short base is still available to cover on an in-line print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze history on prints is visible. The four reactions were all inside ±4.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public data, partly priced. A short base near 10% of float with shorts already covering 10% is not crowded. It is filed small as the mechanism that shrinks any negative.
findings.independence: The baseline options block (skew -4.25, put/call OI 0.12) is a different source pointing the same way.

Its multi-list options capture and Q4-to-date commentary will be read across to MIAX during the first full session. Cboe already disclosed Q3 multi-list ADV of 15.3M in its Oct 5 volume release. findings.why_not_priced: Cannot be priced: it has not happened. It adds variance in the window, not a sign.
findings.independence: Cboe's September volume release (https://finviz.com/news/398922/cboe-global-markets-reports-trading-volume-for-september-2026). Nasdaq's Q3 (2026-10-22, https://mondovisione.com/news/nasdaq-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-strong-execution-drives-12-billion-20261022/) reported Market Services up only 2% y/y, a mild peer read of flat-ish trading revenue.

findings.finding: The Bloomberg financial futures launch is not gaining traction. Financial futures ADV fell from 13,105 contracts in the first 9 launch days (May) to 4,194 (Jul), 1,557 (Aug) and 2,226 (Sep), at a negative rolling RPC of -$1.43 to -$1.66, so MIAX pays to trade. The Futures segment lost $12.7M operating in Q2 and is the growth narrative a call will be asked about. Net of the rest of the company it is small: futures was $5.1M of $141.1M Q2 net revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately visible. Q2's flat futures segment came with a -1.09 reaction alongside a large beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The monthly releases print it, but it has drawn little coverage. A Barchart piece framed the launch as the test of the narrative (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1724598/miax-s-bloomberg-futures-launch-will-either-justify-the-narrative-or-expose-it). Small in dollars, so sized small.
findings.independence: Same IR file as finding 1, a different line (futures volume and RPC). The Q2 release (https://www.miaxglobal.com/news/miami-international-holdings-reports-second-quarter-2026-results) gives the $12.7M segment loss.

findings.finding: FY2026 adjusted opex guidance was lowered in August to $260-270M from $265-275M, and the balance sheet carries $660.5M of cash with $1.5M of debt, so interest income and expense discipline partly cushion the RPC shortfall at the EPS line. Management also said in August it had no buyback or dividend plans until the first year as a public company is behind it (IPO August 2025), so a capital-return announcement is possible but unguided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 opex cut came with a -1.09 reaction. There is no capital-return history.
findings.why_not_priced: The opex guide is public and priced. The capital-return option is not in any estimate: management said it would assess after the first public year, which ended in August 2026. Hence the wide upper range.
findings.independence: The Q2 call transcript (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-5-miami-international-holdings-inc-stock/) is where the no-buyback-yet statement sits.

baseline_tension: The primary-document RPC miss points down, against an upside-paid skew (-4.25), a call-heavy chain and a stock already -9.9% over 5 days near its 52-week low. The evidence cuts against the skew and the run-up, so p_up sits only 3 points below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar disputed: EPS $0.35/$0.40/$0.42, revenue $131.9M vs $135.4M): RPC finding capped from -1.5 to -1.0.
Lesson 7 (negative sign against an upside-paid skew, non-crowded 9.5% short): the same cut on the RPC finding was not stacked a second time; p_up moved from 45 to 47.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): futures finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2, because futures is about 4% of net revenue.
Lessons 1 and 8 left the rest standing: the reaction history is damped (median 2.35), so the RPC number gets no thin-coverage enlargement; seven analysts cover the name.
